nodes.norm_label: build and check the plugin helper
nodes.rationale: The helper is built for each system in the core's folder and started once, checking its protocol and a version read from a version resource (on Linux the helper's own parser).

nodes.label: Core installed from a GitHub tag
nodes.norm_label: core installed from a github tag
nodes.rationale: Built by its prepare script, allowed in package.json allowScripts; a new core release is a new tag; a sibling checkout can be linked to try a change before it is tagged.

nodes.label: Definition of done (tsc, tests, docs, smoke)
nodes.norm_label: definition of done (tsc, tests, docs, smoke)

nodes.label: Guides served at runtime
nodes.rationale: The guides are part of the product, not side notes: served as MCP resources under <scheme>://guides/ and through readServerGuide; this server's list is PRODUCT.guides.

nodes.label: Local-model eval rounds
nodes.rationale: Fixed modding tasks scored with an Ollama-served model; run by the OpenClaw plugin's npm run eval from round 64 (rounds 1-63 ran this server inside OpenClaw), recorded in docs/research/local-model-evals.md.

nodes.label: What this server owns (the MCP side)
nodes.norm_label: what this server owns (the mcp side)

nodes.label: ADR-0007: operating system and mod manager are separate seams
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007: operating system and mod manager are separate seams

nodes.label: Local models through Ollama
nodes.rationale: Ollama's 4k default context is too small for an agent; the model must make real tool calls (gemma4:26b and e4b do, code-completion models write the call as text), so measure a model with the plugin's eval before relying on it.

nodes.label: stdio transport
nodes.rationale: The backend connects before the transport, so a wrong credential or unreachable backend fails at startup with a diagnosis on stderr rather than on the first tool call; stdout is the protocol channel.

nodes.label: healthcheck
nodes.rationale: Defined by the server outside every handler and listed in every profile; reports the profile and what was withheld.

nodes.label: Windows and Linux CI matrix
nodes.rationale: Every push and pull request runs on Windows and Linux, per the core's ADR-0007; Markdown changes run too because the guides and skills are served at runtime and their tests read the real files.

nodes.label: Smoke test over real stdio
nodes.rationale: Fails on anything but JSON-RPC frames on stdout, which no unit test can see; with no game on a runner the server gets a non-existent SKYRIM_MO2_INSTANCE, starts, and healthcheck reports the instance unreadable.

nodes.label: Core-first changes
nodes.rationale: A change to a tool, an answer, a guide or a skill is made in the core, never only here, so every product serving the core stays in sync.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout
nodes.rationale: The server speaks MCP over stdio; anything on stdout that is not a protocol frame corrupts the stream and breaks every tool at once. dotenv 17 did it, so index.ts loads it quiet, and npm run smoke catches that kind.

nodes.label: Retry only what was refused before it ran, once
nodes.norm_label: retry only what was refused before it ran, once
nodes.rationale: isSessionExpired() answers true only for errors that prove nothing was applied; a credential the backend refused is latched and never retried, because retries lock a password account.

nodes.label: Tool reference is generated
nodes.rationale: After a change to any getTools() in the core, run npm run build && npm run docs:tools here; toolDocs.test.ts fails on a stale reference.

nodes.label: Runs beside the game, no container image
nodes.norm_label: runs beside the game, no container image
nodes.rationale: It reads the instance's files, the game's plugins and a Papyrus compiler from disk, runs the .NET plugin helper and must see a running mod manager, none of which a container reaches without bind-mounting everything at identical paths.

nodes.label: OpenClaw served by the plugin, not this server
nodes.norm_label: openclaw served by the plugin, not this server
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw reads none of a server's instructions, prefixes its tools and hides them behind Tool Search for local models; the plugin serves the same tools under their own names with the instructions and skills.

nodes.label: Manual client registration (Claude Code, VS Code, Claude Desktop)
nodes.norm_label: manual client registration (claude code, vs code, claude desktop)
nodes.rationale: Settings go into .env in the server's folder; a client's registration only says how to start the server, Claude Code at --scope user so the server exists in every folder.

nodes.label: Backend feature nexus-premium
nodes.rationale: downloadNexusFile is withheld where the backend lacks the feature, i.e. without a premium account's NEXUS_API_KEY.

nodes.norm_label: git lfs for project meshes and textures

nodes.norm_label: mcp clients (claude code, claude desktop, vs code)

nodes.label: npm run setup
nodes.rationale: Installs the .NET 10 SDK, builds the server and its helper, finds the mod manager and asks only for what it cannot find, registers the clients, and ends with a healthcheck; it asks before anything it installs, downloads or registers.

nodes.label: Every tool declares annotations
nodes.rationale: The core's contract tests hold every tool to it, and server.test.ts checks the same on the wire.

nodes.label: Profile decides what is listed and routed
nodes.norm_label: profile decides what is listed and routed
nodes.rationale: A tool outside the profile is not callable, so the readonly profile genuinely cannot write.

nodes.label: Care with a real backend (test instance)
nodes.norm_label: care with a real backend (test instance)
nodes.rationale: The server writes into a mod manager's instance: prefer read-only tools, work on a test instance (a Wabbajack instance deletes mods it did not install on its next update), change other people's mods only through patches, ask before deploying into an instance you do not own.

nodes.label: Nexus AI tags (AI-Generated Content, AI Media)
nodes.norm_label: nexus ai tags (ai-generated content, ai media)
nodes.rationale: Since 2026-07-31 AI-Generated Content covers AI-written code (written with Claude) and AI Media covers the banner, tile and page text; a mod without the tags its content needs may be moderated.

nodes.label: Nexus API acceptable-use policy
nodes.rationale: Personal API keys are tolerated for personal use; applications others use must register with Nexus and get a slug for single sign-on, and a page on Nexus makes this an application others use.

nodes.label: Release zip packed by git archive
nodes.norm_label: release zip packed by git archive
nodes.rationale: Packed from a release tag so it holds exactly what is committed; unpacked, npm run setup takes it from there as from a clone.

nodes.label: MCP tool annotations
nodes.rationale: Hints for deciding what needs a human (read-only, writes, destructive, idempotent, reaches outside the backend), not a permission system: nothing is enforced.

nodes.label: GPL-3.0 license
nodes.rationale: GPL-3.0 because Mutagen, the plugin engine, is GPL-3.0.

nodes.label: Mods made as text (one YAML file per record)
nodes.norm_label: mods made as text (one yaml file per record)
nodes.rationale: A project can be kept in git, built into a real plugin and deployed; the Creation Kit stays for what only it can do (placing objects, navmesh) and its work is pulled back into the text.

nodes.label: Work on a test instance
nodes.rationale: Deploys write into the instance's mods and profile; a portable Mod Organizer on a clean game is the safe place to learn, and a Wabbajack-installed instance deletes every mod it did not install on update.

nodes.label: Core ToolError becomes McpError
nodes.rationale: The tools are the core's: nothing here builds a tool's envelope; serializeResult passes the core's through, and handleError turns a ToolError into an McpError with the same code and message.

nodes.label: Host allow-list
nodes.rationale: Defence in depth for the rebinding case where the attacker's name resolved to this server.

nodes.label: Origin allow-list
nodes.rationale: Binding to loopback is no access control against DNS rebinding and a reverse proxy cannot help; a page cannot forge the Origin header, so a disallowed Origin gets 403 while requests with no Origin (non-browser MCP clients) pass.

nodes.label: Per-session rate limit (token bucket)
nodes.rationale: One agent in a loop looks like healthy traffic from the front and can take a shared backend down for everyone; over the limit answers 429 with Retry-After.

nodes.label: server.json declares every variable read
nodes.rationale: serverManifest.test.ts holds this server's and the core's declarations together.

nodes.label: Path settings read like a POSIX shell
nodes.norm_label: path settings read like a posix shell
nodes.rationale: Neither .env nor a client's env block passes through a shell, so the core's pathSettings.ts resolves ~, $VAR and ${VAR:-default} on every system; %USERPROFILE%, $(...) and Windows paths on Linux are refused.

nodes.label: russo-2025 papyrus-compiler (Linux)
nodes.rationale: The Creation Kit's compiler is a Windows program; in rare cases this one's output differs byte for byte, not in behaviour.

nodes.label: Wine prefix resolution (SKYRIM_WINE_PREFIX)
nodes.rationale: Mod Organizer writes Windows paths into ModOrganizer.ini; the server follows each drive letter's dosdevices link in the prefix Mod Organizer runs in.

nodes.label: pullProject
nodes.rationale: Refuses while the project folder has uncommitted changes, so what the pull changes can be reviewed with git diff and undone.

nodes.label: Answer ceiling enforced centrally
nodes.rationale: serializeResult() is the single funnel every answer passes through, so the core's responseBudget.ts covers a tool added tomorrow without being told.

nodes.label: SKYRIM_ACCEPTED_TOKENS allow-list
nodes.rationale: There is no remote API behind the server (the backend is a Mod Organizer instance on this machine), so the token list is the whole authority; unset, nobody is accepted.

nodes.label: Deploying with Amethyst open or closed
nodes.norm_label: deploying with amethyst open or closed
nodes.rationale: Closed, the server runs Amethyst's own CLI deploy; open, the answer asks for Refresh then Deploy, because deploying behind its window would race it.

nodes.label: Per-session bearer token
nodes.rationale: createBackend(env, { bearerToken }) builds one backend per session, so two people connecting at once get two independent sessions, never one shared credential.

nodes.label: Close Mod Organizer before deploying (Proton)
nodes.rationale: Mod Organizer holds the profile in memory and writes it back on exit; under Proton the server cannot yet tell it to re-read, so deployProject refuses while this instance's Mod Organizer runs.

nodes.label: Session bound to its bearer token
nodes.norm_label: session bound to its bearer token
nodes.rationale: A session id is a routing key, not a credential, per the MCP specification; every request of a session must present the token that opened it, and only a digest of the token is kept.

nodes.label: TLS terminated in front of the server
nodes.norm_label: tls terminated in front of the server
nodes.rationale: Bearer tokens must not cross a network in clear text.

nodes.label: Vanilla script sources (Scripts.zip)
nodes.rationale: Unpacked into Data with nothing deployed in Amethyst; unpacked while a profile is deployed, Amethyst would count the files as runtime output and move them to its overwrite folder.
